name: Google Cloud Spanner
tagline: Google's globally consistent, horizontally scaling SQL service with graph, vector and full-text built in.
description: Spanner is Google Cloud's fully managed distributed SQL database, the external version of the system that backs Google's own ads and payments infrastructure. It shards data automatically, replicates it with Paxos, and uses TrueTime-synchronized clocks to give externally consistent transactions across regions with a 99.999% SLA on multi-region configurations. Beyond relational tables it now offers Spanner Graph (ISO GQL), vector search, full-text search and a PostgreSQL-dialect interface. Choose it when you need effectively unlimited write scale with strong consistency and are comfortable committing to Google Cloud; for small apps its minimum footprint and pricing are hard to justify.

pricing.notes: Billed per processing unit/node-hour by edition (Standard, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus) plus storage; a 90-day free trial instance is available but not a permanent free tier.

scale.notes: Automatic split-based sharding; granular instances start at 100 processing units; multi-region configs offer 99.999% availability.

strengths: External consistency across regions backed by TrueTime and Paxos
No manual sharding: splits and rebalancing happen automatically
Graph (GQL), vector and full-text search in the same database
Stale reads and point-in-time recovery up to the version retention window
Online schema changes with no maintenance windows
weaknesses: Google Cloud only for the managed service (Spanner Omni is the self-run option)
Expensive at small scale compared with Cloud SQL or Postgres
No triggers or stored procedures; PostgreSQL dialect is a subset
Schema and key design (interleaving, avoiding hotspots) matters a lot for performance
useCases: Global financial ledgers and payment systems
Gaming backends with worldwide player state
Inventory and supply-chain systems of record
Identity and metadata services at very high write rates
notIdealFor: Small or hobby applications on a tight budget
Multi-cloud or on-premises requirements (consider Spanner Omni)
Heavy procedural logic in the database
